To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of the rough air-water interface on radiative transfer are significant for the range of parameters considered in this study, that our analytical model for radiative transmission and reflection functions provides an accurate approximation to the Monte Carlo simulations, that the approximation of the bidirectional reflection functions by the well-known analytical model of Cox and Munk [1968] is not valid for all parameters, and that the analytical model developed in this research is more accurate for the parameters considered in this research.
the effects of a randomly rough interface on the reflected and transmitted radiative fluxes are significant and can be approximated by a perturbative model.

the radiative transfer model developed in this dissertation is capable of accurately describing the effects of a randomly rough interface on the reflected and transmitted radiations due to a source in an optical medium above a material interface with a random surface rough component.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an analytical model for radiative transport through a rough material interface, and the results of the model are validated against Monte Carolo simulations.
the development of an analytical model for the effects of surface roughness on the reflected and transmitted radiative transfer in the atmosphere and ocean.
the development of a new model for the radiative transfer of light through an air-water interface with a rough surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the analytical model presented in this thesis accurately predicts the effects of surface roughness on the radiative transfer process and is an excellent candidate for future implementation in a radiative transfer code for remote sensing.
the proposed analytical models for radiative transport in the ocean are valid and accurate.
this paper provides an analytical model for radiative energy transfer in the ocean-atmosphere system that includes the effects of surface roughness on the reflected and transmitted radiative flux.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a rigorous and tractable model for the radiative transfer of light in an oceanic environment has been derived.
we have developed a formal analytical solution to a radiative transfer problem that includes the effects of a material discontinuity.
we have developed an analytical model for the radiative transfer in the atmosphere and water that includes the effects of the random surface roughness on the material interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of a material interface with a rough surface are significant for remote sensing and must be considered in radiative transfer models.
the radiative transfer model can account for the effects due to a rough material interface in a physically meaningful way, which is important for applications in remote sensing of the ocean surface.
the radiance field is strongly influenced by the roughness of the air-water interface, and this effect can be accounted for in analytical models for radiative transport in the atmosphere and water.
